s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of involuntary movements in an elderly patient with a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
salient_findings: Involuntary movements of the left upper and lower limbs
Slow response and reduced muscle strength in the left limbs
Positive tendon reflexes in the left limbs
Abnormal blood glucose level
High-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on brain MRI
key_facts: The patient is an 80-year-old woman
She has a history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
She presented with involuntary movements of her left upper and lower limbs
The symptoms have been present for more than 10 days
She had a slow response on neurological examination
She had reduced muscle strength in her left limbs
She had positive tendon reflexes in her left limbs
Her blood glucose level was 8.59 mmol/L
Her hemoglobin A1c was 7.43%
Noncontrast CT of the head showed slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions
Brain MRI demonstrated high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

raw.rationale: The patient's history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus, combined with the presence of high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on brain MRI and slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions on noncontrast CT of the head, supports this diagnosis. The patient's symptoms of involuntary movements, slow response, reduced muscle strength, and positive tendon reflexes are also consistent with diabetic striatal disease.

rejected.label: Hemiballismus
rejected.why: Hemiballismus is characterized by involuntary, violent, and large-amplitude movements, which is not exactly matching the patient's symptoms of continuous, irregular involuntary movements of variable amplitude.

rejected.label: Chorea-acanthocytosis
rejected.why: Chorea-acanthocytosis is a rare genetic disorder characterized by chorea, acanthocytosis, and other systemic features, which are not mentioned in the patient's presentation.

rejected.label: Huntington's disease
rejected.why: Huntington's disease typically presents with a combination of chorea, cognitive decline, and psychiatric symptoms, which are not all present in this patient's case.

rejected.label: Wilson's disease
rejected.why: Wilson's disease is a genetic disorder that leads to copper accumulation in the brain and liver, but the patient's presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation
rejected.why: This condition is characterized by iron accumulation in the brain, which is not directly supported by the patient's imaging findings.

rejected.label: Pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration
rejected.why: This is a rare genetic disorder that leads to iron accumulation in the brain, but the patient's presentation and imaging findings do not specifically suggest this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Basal ganglia calcification
rejected.why: While the patient's imaging findings show increased density in the bilateral striatal regions, the clinical presentation and other findings are more consistent with diabetic striatal disease than basal ganglia calcification alone.

rejected.label: Huntington's disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and symptoms do not align with the typical presentation of Huntington's disease, which usually starts at a younger age and includes a broader range of cognitive, psychiatric, and motor symptoms.
